claims.text: Rumi's major works, the Masnavi and the Divan-e Shams, are mainly in Persian, not Turkish, Arabic or Greek, though a few of his verses use those languages.
Rumi was a 13th-century poet who spent most of his life in Konya, in Anatolia.
Persian was a major language of poetry and learning across much of the region in Rumi's time.
The name Rumi means 'from Rum', the name Persian and Arabic writers used for Anatolia, land once ruled by the Eastern Roman Empire.
